title: They Are Here: Alien Abduction Horror for PS5 Under $30
excerpt: This indie alien horror game brings X-Files-era scares to PS5 for $29.99. Weaponless survival with camcorder investigation—but try the demo first.
content:
What Is They Are Here: Alien Abduction Horror?

They Are Here: Alien Abduction Horror is a first-person survival horror game exclusive to PlayStation 5, priced at $29.99. You play as journalist Taylor Fox investigating strange phenomena at Sherman Farm, documenting evidence of alien activity through exploration and stealth. The game draws inspiration from 90s and early 2000s alien conspiracy media, offering a cinematic, story-driven experience with full English voiceover.

  • PlayStation 5 exclusive, single-player only
  • No weapons or combat—survival through hiding, timing, and awareness
  • Camcorder mechanic for documenting evidence and encounters
  • Three main locations: abandoned farmstead, eerie woodlands, and secret government facility
  • Atmospheric horror focused on investigation rather than action

The Camcorder Investigation Mechanic Sets It Apart

The core gameplay revolves around using a camcorder to document strange phenomena and alien encounters as you search for clues, hidden recordings, and evidence throughout the environment. This mechanic positions you as an observer rather than a combatant, emphasizing documentation and investigation over traditional horror game interactions. You'll explore the farmstead, surrounding woods, and a top-secret government facility while piecing together what happened at Sherman Farm.

No Weapons, No Combat—Pure Survival Horror

They Are Here commits fully to defenseless survival horror. You have no weapons, no allies, and no means of fighting back against threats. Success depends entirely on stealth, environmental awareness, proper timing, and finding places to hide when danger appears. This approach aligns the game with titles like Outlast and Alien: Isolation, where evasion and observation are your only tools for survival.

Who Should Consider This Game (And Who Should Skip It)

This game targets a specific audience: horror completists who've exhausted AAA offerings and crave X-Files-era alien conspiracy atmosphere. If you enjoy story-driven, atmospheric horror with investigation mechanics and don't mind weaponless gameplay, this might appeal to you.

Skip this game if you:

  • Prefer action-heavy horror with combat options
  • Want multiplayer or co-op experiences
  • Expect the production values and polish of $60-70 AAA titles
  • Need extensive critical consensus before purchasing
  • Prefer sci-fi shooters or low-intensity experiences

The Biggest Caveat: Zero Critical Reviews

As of now, They Are Here has zero critic reviews on Metacritic and no established quality consensus from professional reviewers. While limited community discussion around the demo mentions positive impressions of atmosphere, sound design, and visuals, individual demo feedback cannot substitute for comprehensive critical analysis of the full game.

This absence of reviews represents significant risk for a $30 purchase. The game may deliver exactly what it promises, or it may suffer from technical issues, pacing problems, or unsatisfying conclusions that reviews would typically reveal. Without this coverage, you're buying based on concept and marketing materials alone.

How It Compares to Outlast and Alien: Isolation

They Are Here shares structural DNA with established horror titles: the weaponless evasion of Outlast, the sci-fi investigation atmosphere of Alien: Isolation, and the camcorder documentation angle familiar from found-footage horror games. However, this is an indie production at a third of the AAA price point, so expectations should account for budget constraints in voice acting quantity, environmental variety, gameplay length, and technical polish.

The game explicitly positions itself as a cinematic, narrative-driven experience rather than a systems-heavy survival simulator, suggesting a more guided, linear structure than open-ended horror sandboxes.

Where to Buy They Are Here for PS5

They Are Here: Alien Abduction Horror is available for PlayStation 5 at $29.99. Before purchasing, note that release date information has shown inconsistencies across retailers, so verify current availability. If a demo is accessible on the PlayStation Store, downloading it first is strongly recommended to assess whether the gameplay, atmosphere, and presentation meet your expectations before committing to the full purchase.

For horror completists willing to support indie developers and gamble on an unreviewed title that promises X-Files-era alien scares, this represents a calculated $30 risk—but only after trying the demo first.
